title: Traders Association v. State of Maharashtra
text: The petitioner, a traders' association, filed a writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution challenging a State government order imposing sudden shop closure timings without any notice or opportunity of hearing. The petition alleges violation of the fundamental right to carry on trade and profession under Article 19(1)(g) of the Constitution of India. The High Court under Article 226 issues a writ of mandamus staying the government order. The order was passed without following mandatory procedural requirements. The State may regulate business hours under its police powers, but must follow due process and afford stakeholders an opportunity to be heard. The fundamental right of traders to carry on business cannot be curtailed by an arbitrary executive fiat. The State is directed to issue fresh notice and conduct consultations before issuing any revised shop closure order.
